diseases.dengue: Dengue is common in Kathmandu. High fever, headache, and joint pain are key symptoms. Please see a doctor immediately. Hospitalization may be needed if platelets drop.
diseases.malaria: Malaria causes recurring fever and chills. Seek medical advice at a nearby hospital. Avoid mosquito bites by using nets.
diseases.cholera: Cholera causes severe diarrhea and dehydration. Rehydrate with ORS and visit a clinic quickly. Ensure your water is boiled.
diseases.typhoid: Typhoid involves prolonged fever and abdominal pain. Requires antibiotics under medical supervision. Search for a nearby hospital for blood tests.
diseases.tuberculosis: TB causes persistent cough, weight loss, and night sweats. Free treatment is available at many government hospitals like TUTH or Bir.
diseases.diabetes: Manage blood sugar through diet, exercise, and meds. You can find Insulin and Metformin in our Medicines section.
diseases.hypertension: High blood pressure requires regular monitoring. Avoid excessive salt and manage stress. Check the Map for specialist clinics.
diseases.asthma: Use inhalers as prescribed. Avoid dust and pollution in Kathmandu. Find inhalers in our Medicines database.
diseases.migraine: Severe headaches, often with nausea. Rest in a dark room and use pain relievers. If chronic, see a neurologist.
diseases.gastritis: Common in Nepal due to spicy foods. Avoid oily food and take antacids. Consult a GI specialist if symptoms persist.
diseases.jaundice: Indicates liver issues. Rest, drink plenty of water, and avoid fat. Seek medical advice if you notice yellow eyes.
diseases.influenza: Common flu requires rest and hydration. Paracetamol manages fever. If breathing gets difficult, seek help.
diseases.measles: High fever and rash. Highly contagious. Isolate the patient and seek pediatric advice.
diseases.pneumonia: Lung infection causing cough and shortness of breath. Often requires antibiotics and sometimes oxygen.
diseases.rabies: Fatal if untreated. If bitten by a dog, wash with soap and get the anti-rabies vaccine immediately at Sukraraj Hospital (Teku).
diseases.tetanus: Caused by bacteria in soil/rust. Ensure Tetanus toxoid vaccination every 10 years, especially after injuries.
diseases.sinusitis: Infection of sinuses causing facial pain and congestion. Steam inhalation and saline sprays help.
diseases.eczema: Chronic skin condition causing itching and redness. Use moisturizers and avoid triggers.
diseases.epilepsy: Neurological disorder involving seizures. Requires long-term medication and safety precautions.
diseases.glaucoma: Increased eye pressure leads to vision loss. Regular eye checkups are vital. See an Ophthalmologist at Tilganga.
diseases.hepatitis: Liver inflammation (A, B, C). A and E are waterborne. Avoid street food during monsoon.
diseases.kidney stones: Causes severe lower back pain. Drink plenty of water. Surgery or lithotripsy may be needed.
diseases.obesity: Risk factor for many diseases. Balanced diet and lifestyle changes are key recommendations.
diseases.tonsillitis: Sore throat and swollen tonsils. Gargarling with warm salt water provides relief. See an ENT if severe.
diseases.urinary tract infection: Causes painful urination. Drink cranberry juice and see a doctor for antibiotics.
diseases.zika virus: Transmitted by mosquitoes. Causes mild fever and rash. Dangerous for pregnant women.
diseases.chickenpox: Causes itchy rash and fever. Highly contagious. Calamine lotion and rest are advised.
diseases.conjunctivitis: Pink eye. Highly contagious. Wash hands frequently and use antibiotic eye drops if prescribed.
diseases.food poisoning: Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Stay hydrated with ORS. Avoid contaminated food.
diseases.bronchitis: Inflammation of bronchial tubes. Causes persistent cough. Avoid smoking and pollution.
diseases.arthritis: Joint inflammation and stiffness. Physical therapy and anti-inflammatories help.
diseases.anemia: Low red blood cell count. Increase iron intake through green leafy vegetables and meat.
diseases.hiv/aids: Immune system condition. Requires ART (Anti-Retroviral Therapy). Support and counseling are vital.
diseases.cataract: Clouding of the eye lens. Restores vision through a simple surgery. Visit Tilganga for world-class care.
diseases.diarrhea: Frequent loose stools. Lead to dehydration. Use ORS immediately.
diseases.food allergy: Immediate reaction to certain foods (peanuts, milk). Use EpiPen for severe reactions.
diseases.skin allergy: Itchy bumps or hives. Antihistamines provide relief. Identify the trigger.
diseases.scabies: Itchy skin condition caused by mites. Requires topical treatment for the whole family.
diseases.psoriasis: Autoimmune skin condition causing scaly patches. Managed with topical creams and light therapy.
diseases.kidney failure: Requires dialysis or transplant. Regular checkups for diabetic patients are crucial.
diseases.meningitis: Inflammation of brain membranes. High fever and stiff neck. Medical emergency.
diseases.dengue fever: See 'Dengue'. Focus on rest and hydration. No specific cure, only management.
diseases.common cold: Viral infection. Rest, fluids, and vitamin C. Usually clears in a week.
diseases.food sensitivity: Less severe than allergy but causes discomfort like bloating.
diseases.toothache: Clean with warm water. See a dentist. Avoid very hot or cold foods.
diseases.stomach ache: Generic pain. Could be gas, acidity, or something serious. Monitor severity.
diseases.fainting: Lay person down, lift legs. Ensure fresh air. Seek help if they don't wake up quickly.
diseases.sunburn: Skin damage from UV rays. Apply aloe vera and stay cool.
diseases.insomnia: Difficulty sleeping. Establish a routine. Avoid caffeine before bed.
diseases.anxiety: Excessive worry. Deep breathing and counseling help. Consult a mental health professional.
diseases.depression: Persistent sadness. Professional therapy and support clusters are effective.
diseases.acidity: Burning sensation in chest. Avoid spicy food and eat smaller meals.
diseases.back pain: Often caused by posture or strain. Exercise and heat packs provide relief.
diseases.burns: Run cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice or butter. Cover with sterile wrap.
diseases.cuts: Apply pressure to stop bleeding. Clean with antiseptic and bandage.
diseases.dog bite: Immediate risk of rabies. See 'Rabies' section for emergency steps.
diseases.fracture: Suspected broken bone. Immobilize the limb and go to the nearest X-ray facility.
diseases.poisoning: Seek immediate help. Do not induce vomiting unless told by a professional.
diseases.snake bite: Stay calm and still to slow venom spread. Do not cut or suck. Go to a hospital with anti-venom.
diseases.sprain: RICE method: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation.
diseases.heart attack: Chest pain, shortness of breath. Call 102 immediately and take aspirin if available.
diseases.stroke: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty. Time is critical. Go to a hospital immediately.
diseases.heat stroke: High body temp, confusion. Move to shade and cool down with water. Emergency.
diseases.seizure: Protect the person from injury. Do not put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure.
diseases.asthma attack: Difficulty breathing. Use emergency inhaler. If no relief in 10 mins, seek help.
diseases.allergic reaction: Itching, swelling. Use antihistamines. If throat swells (Anaphylaxis), call 102.
diseases.bleeding: Heavy blood loss. Apply firm pressure. If limb, elevate above heart.
diseases.choking: Perform Heimlich maneuver if they cannot cough or breathe. Call for help.
diseases.head injury: Check for consciousness and vomiting. Could be a concussion. Monitor closely.
diseases.eye injury: Do not rub. Flush gently with water. See a specialist immediately.
diseases.fever in child: Check temp. Use child-appropriate Paracetamol dosage. Keep hydrated.
diseases.vomiting in child: Risk of dehydration. Give tiny sips of ORS frequently.
diseases.cough: Common symptom. Honey and lemon can soothe 'dry' coughs.
diseases.sore throat: Gargle salt water. Stay hydrated with warm fluids.
diseases.earache: Could be infection. Do not insert objects. Use warm compress.
diseases.rash: Redness or bumps. Could be allergy or infection. Observe if it spreads.
diseases.stings: Bee or wasp. Remove stinger and apply cold pack. Watch for allergies.
